editorial:
Imagine being handed a job where you have to put a price tag on a human life. That is exactly what happens to Kenneth Feinberg, a high-powered lawyer who gets picked to run the 9/11 Victim Compensation Fund. At first, he treats the whole thing like a math problem, focusing on rules and paperwork while ignoring the pain of the families. You get to see him struggle as he realizes that these people are not just files on a desk, but heartbroken families who feel like the government is trying to cheat them out of their grief.

What really makes this work is the acting, as you watch the main character change from a cold professional into someone who actually cares. The movie moves at a steady pace and stays grounded in reality, though some parts might feel a bit slow if you are looking for big action scenes. If you like dramas that make you think about right and wrong, you should definitely give this a shot.
endingExplained: By the end, the lawyer stops following the strict rules and starts listening to the families. He realizes that the government's formulas were unfair to those who lost everything. He fights the bureaucracy to make sure more people get the money they deserve. The movie wraps up by showing his personal growth, as he learns that you cannot put a price on a life, but you can show respect through fairness and empathy.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves true stories and legal dramas.
